# The apt package set the site build needs — the ONE definition.
# .github/workflows/site.yml installs exactly this list and keys its .deb
# cache on this file's hash, so editing it (even a comment) re-keys the cache
# automatically — there is no version suffix to remember to bump. ./setup.sh
# installs the same set locally, probe-by-probe; keep the two in step.
#
# Keep the list lean: it is the biggest single cost of a cold CI run, and a
# slow Ubuntu mirror can stall a download for 15+ minutes.
#
# texlive-science (4 MB) is absent ON PURPOSE: it hard-depends on
# texlive-lang-greek (75 MB) and its only user here was stmaryrd, for two
# bracket glyphs now built from kernel pieces. Likewise alphaurl.bst is
# vendored at tex/alphaurl.bst (found via BSTINPUTS) rather than pulled in.

texlive-latex-extra
texlive-pictures
texlive-fonts-recommended

# Scalable CM fonts — needed by microtype's font expansion under [T1]{fontenc}.
cm-super

# pdftocairo/pdftoppm for the tikz-SVG and thumbnail pipeline.
poppler-utils

# The two halves a biblatex document needs (C.2's deck): biber, the backend
# that reads the .bib and writes the .bbl, and biblatex.sty itself, which on
# Ubuntu ships ONLY in texlive-bibtex-extra (79 MB — it earns its place; the
# deck's 97 \source{} attributions are built on \DeclareCiteCommand, which has
# no plain-bibtex equivalent). Vendoring biblatex alone does not work: biber
# enforces an exact control-file version, so a pinned copy that satisfies CI's
# biber 2.19 breaks every local build against TeX Live 2024's biber 2.20. The
# distro pair is what keeps style and backend in step.
biber
texlive-bibtex-extra

# Decks \usepackage{lmodern}. Only a *Recommends* of texlive-latex-recommended,
# so --no-install-recommends drops it and the deck build dies on a missing
# lmodern.sty. Named explicitly.
lmodern

# pygmentize: minted shells out to it for syntax-highlighted code in slide
# decks (C.1's). The slides ladder runs pdflatex -shell-escape, scoped to decks
# only — see scripts/build-content.mjs; worksheets keep the sandbox.
python3-pygments
